pr_body:
This PR introduces the `UNSIGNED_LONG` type to QL following its availability in ES (#60050).

The type is mapped to a BigInteger whose value is checked against the UL bounds.

The SQL will now support the type as literal and in the arithmetic functions; the non-arithmetic functions however are unchanged (i.e. they still require a long / int parameter where that is the case).

The type is version-gated: for the driver SQL clients (only) the server checks their version and in case this is lower than the one introducing the UL support, it fails the request, for queries, or simply hidden in catalog functions (similar to how `UNSUPPORTED` is currently treated in the similar case)

The JDBC tests are adjusted to read the (bwc) version of the driver they are run against and selectively disable part of the tests accordingly.

Closes #63312

(I'll look into the latter.)

> 3. Do you think the tests we have so far answer the question "is running SELECT unsigned_long FROM test using an old JDBC driver version handled correctly both server and driver side?"

Yes-ish: the bwc tests can only [go back as far as 7.9.0](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/be86dd5625e805078de56cd1332fa052c569d71e/x-pack/plugin/sql/qa/jdbc/build.gradle#L76). jar hell ensues if trying to go back further (I tried). (FWIW I'll expand ODBC to run bwc tests too and starting from 7.7.0, but those aren't as exhaustive as JDBC's.)

Thanks for the prompt (and generous!) feedback. I hope I've addressed all the raised points.
The UL support in scripts remaining a pending issue, though, that will need to be addressed in parallel, but hope to have this PR ready before then.

> SHOW COLUMNS should behave differently, for consistency, when it comes to different driver versions?

I tend to think that yes, if the user specified an old ("enough") version, we should filter `unsigned_long`s out.
OTOH, I believe the `SHOW`s are pure human-specific commands and a user would not normally issue them  when connecting through a driver. If connecting through the CLI or REST, `unsigned_long`s would not be an issue.

Anyways, unless anyone raises a concern, I'll have `SHOW` be version-aware.

> Anyways, unless anyone raises a concern, I'll have SHOW be version-aware.

This test has been now added.

Additionally, after some more testing, it's obvious that most client applications don't support (or check for) unsigned types.
Advertising `UNSIGNED_LONG` as a `BIGINT` type makes them assume it's signed (although
xDBC APIs allow checking). Consequently I've changed the xDBC type to NUMERIC, which offer more conversion safety.

> I think there is also a problem with scripting in this PR

@Luegg, there was indeed, thanks. Added better test data and hopefully ironed out all issues.

> Use the client version in the analyzer to change the server datatype from known to unknown.

The UL fields' datatype has been changed version dependent (in the IndexResolver, though, where the fields are created).

> Mark the feature as experimental

Sure, the docs PR that'll follow will note this support as experimental.

The argument to `%s` is a `Number` here, can be a fixed point, but can be a floating point too. `%d` [means](x-pack/plugin/sql/jdbc/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/sql/jdbc/TypeConverter.java): `The result is formatted as a decimal integer`, which would result in an `IllegalFormatConversionException` for non-integers. 
Otoh `%s` would have `format` call `.toString()`, which should be safe for any Number.

The original method didn't get renamed, strictly "speaking", but changed to take a Number. But also needed to add a new one (safeDoubleToLong) that takes doubles only. Since they both take doubles, I wanted to avoid the ambiguity.
This check is useful only when NOT doing SELECT * - that is when the consumer specifies each field individually. The two approaches need to be aligned - either we filter all the way or not at all.

In a version-gated answer, the `unsigned_long` fields would appear nowhere in SQL catalog results. So `SELECT *` expansion is consistent with this check. If the user "discovers" the fields "out-of-band" though and explicitly inserts an unsigned_long field in the query, that'll be caught by this check.
Again, I think we do this for other "unsupported" field types too (just not version-gated).

To make sure: I think aligning is great, just not sure on how to improve this, specifically.
